title: Bound state solutions of the Schrödinger equation for the atomic systems interacting with the radial screened Coulomb potential: analytical approximation methods
authors: Fatma Zohra Khaled, Mustafa Moumni, Mokhtar Falek
abstract: We investigate the bound state properties of the hydrogen-like atoms in the radial screened Coulomb potential (RSCP). using three complementary analytical approaches - expectation values with Coulomb and Kratzer reference states, variational optimization with a scaled Kratzer basis, and the Hellmann-Feynman theorem - we derive approximate energy eigenvalues as function of the screening parameter c. Benchmarked against high-precision generalized pseudospectral data, the expectation value-approach with the Kratzer basis achieves relative errors of 0.63% for the first ten s-states at $c=0.1$, while the variational method improves this further. The formalism extends naturally to Positronium, demonstrating its generality for arbitrary reduced-mass systems. The complementary biases of the methods provide robust error estimation for plasma-embedded atoms.
summary: This paper develops and compares three sophisticated analytical methods—expectation values, variational optimization, and the Hellmann-Feynman theorem—to determine the bound state energies of hydrogenic atoms in a screened Coulomb potential. By achieving high accuracy relative to numerical benchmarks, it provides valuable theoretical tools for understanding atomic structure within plasma diagnostics.
main_problem: The study investigates the bound state properties of hydrogen-like atoms when interacting with the radial screened Coulomb potential (RSCP). The goal is to derive approximate energy eigenvalues as a function of the screening parameter.
main_result: The expectation value approach using the Kratzer basis achieved relative errors of 0.63% for the first ten s-states at $c=0.1$, with further improvements possible via variational methods. The formalism is general and applicable to Positronium.
method: Three complementary analytical approaches are employed: expectation values using reference states (Coulomb/Kratzer), variational optimization with a scaled Kratzer basis, and the Hellmann-Feynman theorem for error estimation.
model_or_system: The system is hydrogen-like atoms modeled by the radial Schrödinger equation subjected to the RSCP potential, $V_{RSCP}(r) = -Ze^2/r e^{-c/r}$. This potential models short-range screening effects in plasma environments.
key_observables: Approximate energy eigenvalues ($E_{n,l}$) as a function of the screening parameter $c$.
important_parameters: Screening parameter $c$, quantum numbers $(n, \ell)$, and variational parameters $ eta$. The limit $c 	o 0$ recovers the standard Coulomb result.
main_assumptions: The methods rely on using approximate wavefunctions derived from reference potentials (Coulomb or Kratzer) to evaluate expectation values of the full RSCP Hamiltonian. The Hellmann-Feynman approach requires numerical integration for certain parameters.
paper_structure: The paper systematically details three methods—expectation value, variational, and Hellmann-Feynman—for calculating energy eigenvalues, compares their results against high-precision data, demonstrates the general applicability to Positronium, and concludes with error analysis.
why_interesting: This work provides advanced analytical tools for calculating atomic energy levels in realistic plasma environments where screening effects are crucial. The combination of multiple theoretical approaches offers robust benchmarking for complex quantum systems.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Relative errors (%, logarithmic scale) of the calculated energies for the first ten s states of the hydrogen atom in the RSCP at c = 0.1, measured with respect to the GPS reference values.

Figure 2. Comprehensive comparison of energy eigenvalues for the first three s-states (1s, 2s, 3s) of the hydrogen atom in the RSCP as functions of the screening parameter c. All methods are shown for c values from 0 to 1 with steps of 0.1. GPS reference values are shown at both c = 0.1 and c = 1.0 (diamonds). Symbols: solid lines = Kratzer reference; open circles (◦) = Coulomb reference; filled squares (■) = variational method; filled triangles (▲) = Hellmann–Feynman with Kratzer basis; filled diamonds (♦) = GPS reference.

Figure 3. Comprehensive comparison of energy eigenvalues for higher excited s states (4s, 5s, 6s, and 7s) of the hydrogen atom in the RSCP as functions of the screening parameter c. All methods are shown for c values from 0 to 1 with steps of 0.1. GPS reference values are shown at c = 0.1 (diamonds). Symbols: solid lines = Kratzer reference; open circles (◦) = Coulomb reference; filled squares (■) = variational method; filled triangles (▲) = Hellmann–Feynman with Kratzer basis; filled diamonds (♦) = GPS reference.

Figure 4. Comparison of the EVA with Kratzer basis (solid lines) with the asymptotic approximation of Xu et al. (2024) (dashed lines) for the first three s-states over the range 0 ≤c ≤1. Filled squares (■) show the variational results. Diamonds (♦) indicate GPS reference values at c = 0.1 and c = 1.0.
